{"consolidated_memory":"## Loss Divergence in ml/train/loop.py – Two Separate Incidents

**OCCASION 1: [2026-02-12]**
- File: ml/train/loop.py (ml pipeline side)
- Problem: Loss divergence in the training loop
- Trigger: Appeared only on the first request after a cold start
- Signal: Loss curve turns upward and never returns
- Root cause: Schema drift between the migration and the model
- Fix: Regenerated the model from the migration and pinned the checksum
- PR: #3597 on branch fix/loss-divergence-1
- Reproduction: Train two epochs on the small split
- Outcome: Nightly rollup matched the source counts for 41 days running

**OCCASION 2: [2026-07-03]**
- File: ml/train/loop.py (same area as Occasion 1; context carried over)
- Problem: Loss divergence in the training loop
- Trigger: Appeared only after the client had already retried once
- Signal: Loss curve turns upward and never returns
- Root cause: Missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
- Fix: Added the composite index and backfilled in batches
- PR: #8497 on branch fix/loss-divergence-2
- Reproduction: Train two epochs on the small split
- Outcome: Throughput rose 46 percent, to 309 requests per second

Both incidents had identical signal presentation but different underlying causes (schema drift vs. missing index) and different measured outcomes."}
